newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty slips vs basket, depos extend fall.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty slips vs basket, depos extend fall.

text.p: The Polish zloty softened versus the basket of five western currencies on Thursday after a quick wave of currency buying in the morning, dealers said.
They said the early buying trend, likely speculative in nature, soon faded as no large orders appeared to move the market, which remained driven mainly by dollar/mark changes.
"Market trends, most likely based on speculation, were short-lived today and most deals were done for small amounts," said Marcin Trzykowski of Pekao SA.
The zloty closed at 1.97/1.94 percent from the trading band centre down from Wednesday's close at 2.07/2.02 percent.
It was at 2.8100/08 to the dollar, up from 2.8170/82 on Wednesday and at 1.8642/47 to the mark, down from 1.8535/55.

One-day deposit rates extended their recent fall as banks regained liquidity following a severe cash shortage at the end of October and on Thursday call-money rates formed around the central bank's main 14-day drainage rate, now at 19.15 percent.
Overnight rates closed at 19.00/19.25 percent down from Wednesday's 19.25/19.55 percent, while tomorrow/next were at 19.05/19.35 percent, also down from 19.25/19.55.
The central bank let the maximum rate inch up 0.01 point at today's drainge while cutting the price for its 273-day bills.
Dealers said that today's tightening could be the first step of the central bank's (NBP) previously announced move to converge market rates with official interest rates.
"The NBP may be starting to force up market rates as it said it would do," said one dealer at a large Polish bank.
The central bank lowered the minimum price of its 273-day NBP-bill, available only to domestic banks, by 0.01 to 86.64, but the average yield held flat at 19.97 percent.
Dealers said longer deposit remained high today with 3-week depos bid around 19.45 percent and one-month around 19.40.
